subproblem.title: Small perturbations x + tZ(x) of the identity by a compactly supported C¹ field are bi-Lipschitz bijections with injective derivative (parent steps 1–2)
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ and let Z : ℝ^P → ℝ^P be of class C¹ with compact support. Then there is t₀ > 0 such that for every t ∈ ℝ with |t| < t₀ the map Φ_t(x) := x + tZ(x) satisfies: (i) Φ_t is bijective; (ii) its derivative DΦ_t(x) is an injective linear map for every x ∈ ℝ^P; (iii) there is Λ ≥ 0 such that Φ_t is Λ-Lipschitz and Λ-antilipschitz, i.e. |Φ_t(a) − Φ_t(b)| ≤ Λ|a − b| and |a − b| ≤ Λ|Φ_t(a) − Φ_t(b)| for all a, b ∈ ℝ^P.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (Z : Euclid P → Euclid P), ContDiff ℝ 1 Z → HasCompactSupport Z → ∃ t₀ : ℝ, 0 < t₀ ∧ ∀ t : ℝ, |t| < t₀ → Bijective (fun x => x + t • Z x) ∧ (∀ x, Injective (fderiv ℝ (fun x => x + t • Z x) x)) ∧ ∃ Λ : NNReal, LipschitzWith Λ (fun x => x + t • Z x) ∧ AntilipschitzWith Λ (fun x => x + t • Z x)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. Parent steps 1 (choice of t₀ = 1/(1 + sup‖DZ‖)) and 2 (Φ_t is a diffeomorphism, the two-sided bound (1 − |t|Λ)|a − b| ≤ |Φ(a) − Φ(b)| ≤ (1 + |t|Λ)|a − b|, injectivity, surjectivity by a contraction, invertibility of DΦ) of the supplied proof of codim1_minimizing_piece_area_comparison; Simon Ch. 2, 5.1–5.2 (chapter-02.txt lines 1162–1205: φ_t(x) = x + tX(x) is a 1:1 map of U for small |t|). Here Z is only assumed C¹ (the parent applies it to its C^∞ field Z).
Notation. |·| is the Euclidean norm of ℝ^P and ‖·‖ the operator norm. Write Φ := Φ_t once t is fixed.

Proof.
1. (Bound on DZ.) Z is C¹, so x ↦ DZ(x) is continuous (ContDiff.continuous_fderiv). Z vanishes on the open set ℝ^P ∖ tsupport Z, hence DZ(x) = 0 for x ∉ tsupport Z (the derivative of a function that is locally constant zero). Thus x ↦ ‖DZ(x)‖ is continuous and vanishes outside the compact set tsupport Z, so it is bounded: L := sup_x ‖DZ(x)‖ ∈ [0, ∞) (if tsupport Z = ∅, L = 0).
2. (Z is L-Lipschitz.) Z is differentiable on the convex set ℝ^P with ‖DZ(x)‖ ≤ L for all x, so by the mean value inequality |Z(a) − Z(b)| ≤ L|a − b| for all a, b (Mathlib lipschitzWith_of_nnnorm_fderiv_le).
3. (Choice of t₀.) Put t₀ := 1/(1 + L) > 0. Fix t ∈ ℝ with |t| < t₀ and put κ := |t|L. Then 0 ≤ κ ≤ |t|(1 + L) < 1.
4. (Two-sided bound.) For a, b ∈ ℝ^P, Φ(a) − Φ(b) = (a − b) + t(Z(a) − Z(b)) and |t(Z(a) − Z(b))| ≤ |t|L|a − b| = κ|a − b| by step 2. By the triangle inequality,
 (4.1) (1 − κ)|a − b| ≤ |Φ(a) − Φ(b)| ≤ (1 + κ)|a − b|.
5. (Lipschitz and antilipschitz.) Let Λ := max(1 + κ, (1 − κ)^{-1}), a nonnegative real number (1 − κ > 0). By the right half of (4.1), Φ is (1 + κ)-Lipschitz, hence Λ-Lipschitz. By the left half, |a − b| ≤ (1 − κ)^{-1}|Φ(a) − Φ(b)| ≤ Λ|Φ(a) − Φ(b)|; in the extended-distance form used by AntilipschitzWith this reads edist a b ≤ Λ·edist(Φ a, Φ b). So Φ is Λ-Lipschitz and Λ-antilipschitz, which is (iii).
6. (Injectivity.) If Φ(a) = Φ(b), the left half of (4.1) gives (1 − κ)|a − b| ≤ 0, so a = b because 1 − κ > 0.
7. (Surjectivity.) Fix y ∈ ℝ^P and define T(x) := y − tZ(x). By step 2, |T(a) − T(b)| = |t||Z(a) − Z(b)| ≤ κ|a − b| with κ < 1, so T is a contraction of the complete metric space ℝ^P. By the Banach fixed point theorem (Mathlib ContractingWith.fixedPoint with ContractingWith.fixedPoint_isFixedPt) there is x with T(x) = x, i.e. x + tZ(x) = y, i.e. Φ(x) = y. With step 6, Φ is bijective, which is (i).
8. (Derivative.) Φ is differentiable everywhere with DΦ(x) = I + tDZ(x) (derivative of the identity plus a constant multiple of Z). If DΦ(x)v = 0 then v = −tDZ(x)v, so |v| ≤ |t|‖DZ(x)‖|v| ≤ κ|v|; since κ < 1 this forces |v| = 0. Hence DΦ(x) is injective for every x, which is (ii).
9. (Conclusion.) Steps 5–8 hold for every t with |t| < t₀, and t₀ > 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: L := sup‖DZ‖ < ∞ since DZ is continuous and vanishes off the compact tsupport Z; Z is L-Lipschitz by the mean value inequality.
Λ := max(1 + κ, (1 − κ)^{-1}) makes Φ Λ-Lipschitz and Λ-antilipschitz; injectivity follows.
Surjectivity: the Banach fixed point of the contraction x ↦ y − tZ(x) solves Φ(x) = y.
DΦ(x) = I + tDZ(x) with ‖tDZ(x)‖ ≤ κ < 1 is injective.

subproblem.title: The image of an embedded C¹ submanifold under an antilipschitz C¹ bijection of ℝ^P with injective derivative is an embedded C¹ submanifold with tangent spaces DΦ(T_xN)
subproblem.statement: Let P, d ∈ ℕ, let N ⊆ ℝ^P be an embedded d-dimensional C¹ submanifold in the sense of Simon Ch. 2, 4.1 (IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 1 d N), and let Φ : ℝ^P → ℝ^P be a C¹ bijection such that DΦ(x) is injective for every x and Φ is Λ-antilipschitz for some Λ ≥ 0 (|a − b| ≤ Λ|Φ(a) − Φ(b)|). Then Φ(N) is an embedded d-dimensional C¹ submanifold, and for every x ∈ N the tangent space of Φ(N) at Φ(x) (contract tangentSpace: velocities γ′(0) of C¹ curves γ : (−1, 1) → Φ(N) with γ(0) = Φ(x)) is the image DΦ(x)(T_xN) of the tangent space of N at x.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P d : ℕ) (N : Set (Euclid P)) (Φ : Euclid P → Euclid P) (Λ : NNReal), IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 1 d N → ContDiff ℝ 1 Φ → Bijective Φ → (∀ x, Injective (fderiv ℝ Φ x)) → AntilipschitzWith Λ Φ → IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 1 d (Φ '' N) ∧ ∀ x ∈ N, tangentSpace (Φ '' N) (Φ x) = (fderiv ℝ Φ x) '' tangentSpace N x
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. Simon Ch. 2, §4, 4.1–4.3 (chapter-02.txt lines 846–875: local representations ψ : V → W with ψ(V) = W ∩ M, ψ proper, Dψ of rank n; T_yM has basis D_1ψ(x), …, D_nψ(x)). It supplies the fact used in parent step 6 that Φ(M ∩ W) is a piece of the C¹ submanifold Φ(M) with tangent planes DΦ(x)(T_xM). Uses the sibling chart_tangent_space (Submission.chart_tangentSpace_eq_range_fderiv): for a local representation (V, W, ψ) of a set N (V ⊆ ℝ^d, W ⊆ ℝ^P open, ψ C^r on V with r ≥ 1, injective on V, ψ(V) = W ∩ N, V ∩ ψ^{-1}(K) compact for compact K ⊆ W, Dψ injective on V) and v ∈ V, tangentSpace N (ψ(v)) = range Dψ(v).

Proof.
1. (Φ is a homeomorphism.) Φ is continuous, being C¹. Let Φ^{-1} be the inverse of the bijection Φ. For a, b ∈ ℝ^P, antilipschitzness applied to Φ^{-1}(a), Φ^{-1}(b) gives |Φ^{-1}(a) − Φ^{-1}(b)| ≤ Λ|a − b|, so Φ^{-1} is Lipschitz, hence continuous. Consequently Φ(O) = (Φ^{-1})^{-1}(O) is open for every open O, and Φ^{-1}(K) = Φ^{-1}''K is compact for every compact K (continuous image of a compact set).
2. (Charts of Φ(N).) Let y′ ∈ Φ(N), say y′ = Φ(y) with y ∈ N. By IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 1 d N at y there are open V ⊆ ℝ^d and W ⊆ ℝ^P with y ∈ W and ψ : ℝ^d → ℝ^P such that ψ is C¹ on V, injective on V, ψ(V) = W ∩ N, V ∩ ψ^{-1}(K) is compact for every compact K ⊆ W, and Dψ(z) is injective for every z ∈ V. Put W′ := Φ(W) and ψ′ := Φ ∘ ψ. We verify the defining conditions for (V, W′, ψ′) at y′:
 (a) V is open; W′ is open by step 1; y′ = Φ(y) ∈ Φ(W) = W′.
 (b) ψ′ is C¹ on V: Φ is C¹ on ℝ^P and ψ is C¹ on V (ContDiff.comp_contDiffOn).
 (c) ψ′ is injective on V: ψ is injective on V and Φ is injective.
 (d) ψ′(V) = Φ(ψ(V)) = Φ(W ∩ N) = Φ(W) ∩ Φ(N) = W′ ∩ Φ(N); the third equality holds because Φ is injective (Set.image_inter).
 (e) Properness: let K ⊆ W′ be compact. Then K′ := Φ^{-1}(K) is compact (step 1), and K′ ⊆ W: if Φ(z) ∈ K ⊆ Φ(W), then Φ(z) = Φ(w) for some w ∈ W and z = w by injectivity. Since V ∩ ψ′^{-1}(K) = V ∩ ψ^{-1}(Φ^{-1}(K)) = V ∩ ψ^{-1}(K′), it is compact by the properness of ψ.
 (f) Let z ∈ V. As V is open and ψ is C¹ on V, ψ is differentiable at z; Φ is differentiable at ψ(z). By the chain rule Dψ′(z) = DΦ(ψ(z)) ∘ Dψ(z), a composition of two injective linear maps, hence injective.
 Since y′ ∈ Φ(N) was arbitrary, Φ(N) is an embedded d-dimensional C¹ submanifold (IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 1 d (Φ '' N)).
3. (Tangent spaces.) Let x ∈ N. Take a chart (V, W, ψ) of N at x as in step 2, and v ∈ V with ψ(v) = x (possible since x ∈ W ∩ N = ψ(V)). By chart_tangent_space (with r = 1) applied to N and (V, W, ψ): T_xN = range Dψ(v). By step 2 (a)–(f), (V, W′, ψ′) satisfies all hypotheses of chart_tangent_space for the set Φ(N), and ψ′(v) = Φ(x); hence
 T_{Φ(x)}Φ(N) = range Dψ′(v) = range(DΦ(x) ∘ Dψ(v)) = DΦ(x)(range Dψ(v)) = DΦ(x)(T_xN).
 This is the second conclusion. ∎
proof_key_steps: Antilipschitz + bijective + continuous: Φ is a homeomorphism (Φ^{-1} is Λ-Lipschitz).
For a chart (V, W, ψ) of N at y, (V, Φ(W), Φ∘ψ) is a chart of Φ(N) at Φ(y): open, C¹, injective, image Φ(W) ∩ Φ(N), proper via Φ^{-1}(K) compact, injective derivative by the chain rule.
chart_tangent_space for both charts: T_{Φ(x)}Φ(N) = range D(Φ∘ψ)(v) = DΦ(x)(range Dψ(v)) = DΦ(x)(T_xN).

subproblem.title: At each of its points an embedded C¹ submanifold (cut by an open set) has its tangent space as approximate tangent space (Simon Ch. 3, 1.4 and proof of 1.6)
subproblem.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ with m ≥ 1, let N ⊆ ℝ^P be an embedded m-dimensional C¹ submanifold (IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 1 m N), W ⊆ ℝ^P open, x ∈ N ∩ W, and Q a linear subspace of ℝ^P whose underlying set is the tangent space T_xN (contract tangentSpace N x). Then Q is the approximate tangent space of N ∩ W at x in the sense of Simon Ch. 3, 1.4 (HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt m (N ∩ W) x Q): dim Q = m, and for every continuous compactly supported f : ℝ^P → ℝ, ∫_{η_{x,r}(N ∩ W)} f dH^m → ∫_Q f dH^m as r ↓ 0, where η_{x,r}(y) = r^{-1}(y − x) and H^m = μHE[m].

Since F(D ∩ F^{-1}(E)) = F(D) ∩ E, this says that the Borel measures E ↦ H^m(F(G) ∩ E) and E ↦ ∫_{G ∩ F^{-1}(E)} J(DF) du agree for every Borel G ⊆ D, i.e. H^m⌞F(G) is the image of J(DF)·L^m⌞G under F (in Lean, Measure.map F (…) with the a.e.-measurability of F on G supplied by ContinuousOn.aemeasurable, since Measure.map of a non-a.e.-measurable map is 0; F(A) is Borel for Borel A ⊆ D by MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn); hence (★) ∫_{F(G)} g dH^m = ∫_G g(F(u)) J(DF(u)) du for every bounded Borel g : ℝ^P → ℝ when the right side has an integrable bound (apply the measure identity to g⁺ and g⁻).

Proof.
1. (Chart; dimension of Q.) By IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 1 m N at x there are open V ⊆ ℝ^m, W₀ ⊆ ℝ^P with x ∈ W₀ and ψ : ℝ^m → ℝ^P, C¹ on V, injective on V, with ψ(V) = W₀ ∩ N, V ∩ ψ^{-1}(K) compact for every compact K ⊆ W₀, and Dψ(v) injective for v ∈ V. Choose v₀ ∈ V with ψ(v₀) = x and put A := Dψ(v₀). By chart_tangent_space, T_xN = range A; hence Q = range A as subspaces (equal underlying sets). A is injective, so dim Q = m: the first conjunct.
2. (Uniform bounds near v₀.) As m ≥ 1 and A is injective, c₀ := min_{|u|=1}|Au| > 0 (the unit sphere of ℝ^m is compact and nonempty), and |Au| ≥ c₀|u| for all u. By continuity of Dψ at v₀ (ψ is C¹ on the open set V) choose ρ₀ > 0 with B̄_{ρ₀}(v₀) ⊆ V and ‖Dψ(v) − A‖ ≤ c₀/2 for v ∈ B̄_{ρ₀}(v₀). The mean value inequality for v ↦ ψ(v) − Av on the convex set B̄_{ρ₀}(v₀) gives |ψ(v) − ψ(v′) − A(v − v′)| ≤ (c₀/2)|v − v′|, hence
 (2.1) |ψ(v) − ψ(v′)| ≥ (c₀/2)|v − v′| for v, v′ ∈ B̄_{ρ₀}(v₀).
 Moreover v ↦ J(Dψ(v)) is continuous on the compact set B̄_{ρ₀}(v₀), so C_J := max_{B̄_{ρ₀}(v₀)} J(Dψ) < ∞.
3. (Localization.) Choose ε > 0 with B̄_ε(x) ⊆ W ∩ W₀. The set C₁ := (V ∩ ψ^{-1}(B̄_ε(x))) ∖ B_{ρ₀}(v₀) is compact (a closed subset of the compact set V ∩ ψ^{-1}(B̄_ε(x)), properness), so ψ(C₁) is compact (ψ is continuous on V ⊇ C₁). x ∉ ψ(C₁), since ψ(v) = x = ψ(v₀) with v ∈ V forces v = v₀ ∈ B_{ρ₀}(v₀). Let δ := min(ε, dist(x, ψ(C₁))) > 0 (δ := ε if C₁ = ∅). Then
 (3.1) N ∩ B_δ(x) ⊆ ψ(B_{ρ₀}(v₀)) and N ∩ B_δ(x) ⊆ N ∩ W.
 Indeed let y ∈ N with |y − x| < δ ≤ ε; then y ∈ W ∩ W₀ ∩ N, so y = ψ(v) with v ∈ V and ψ(v) ∈ B̄_ε(x); if v ∉ B_{ρ₀}(v₀) then v ∈ C₁ and |y − x| ≥ dist(x, ψ(C₁)) ≥ δ, a contradiction.

 (4.1) η_{x,r}(N ∩ W) ∩ B_R(0) = ψ_r(G′_r).
 ⊇: for u ∈ G′_r, y := ψ(v₀ + ru) ∈ ψ(V) ⊆ N, and |y − x| = r|ψ_r(u)| < rR < δ ≤ ε, so y ∈ W; thus ψ_r(u) = η_{x,r}(y) ∈ η_{x,r}(N ∩ W) ∩ B_R(0). ⊆: if y ∈ N ∩ W and |η_{x,r}(y)| < R, then |y − x| < rR < δ, so by (3.1) y = ψ(v) with v ∈ B_{ρ₀}(v₀); u := (v − v₀)/r ∈ G_r and ψ_r(u) = η_{x,r}(y), so u ∈ G′_r.
 N is Borel (SimonGMT measurableSet_of_isSimonSubmanifold, after unfolding the contract's chart conditions into IsSimonSubmanifold), W is open and η_{x,r} is a homeomorphism, so η_{x,r}(N ∩ W) is Borel. Since f vanishes outside B_R(0), Mathlib setIntegral_eq_of_subset_of_forall_sdiff_eq_zero and (4.1) give

5. (Area formula in the chart.) ψ_r is C¹ on the open set G_r, injective there (ψ is injective on V), and Dψ_r(u) = Dψ(v₀ + ru) (chain rule) is injective. By (2.1), for u ∈ G′_r: R > |ψ_r(u)| = r^{-1}|ψ(v₀ + ru) − ψ(v₀)| ≥ (c₀/2)|u|, so G′_r ⊆ B_{2R/c₀}(0), and J(Dψ_r(u)) ≤ C_J. Hence (★) applies to F = ψ_r, G = G′_r and g = f, and since f(ψ_r(u)) = 0 for u ∈ G_r ∖ G′_r:
 (5.1) ∫_{ψ_r(G′_r)} f dH^m = ∫_{G′_r} f(ψ_r(u)) J(Dψ(v₀ + ru)) du = ∫_{ℝ^m} h_r(u) du, h_r(u) := 1_{G_r}(u) f(ψ_r(u)) J(Dψ(v₀ + ru)).
6. (Domination.) If h_r(u) ≠ 0 then u ∈ G′_r, so |u| < 2R/c₀ (step 5). Hence |h_r(u)| ≤ H(u) := sup|f|·C_J·1_{B_{2R/c₀}(0)}(u) for all u and all r ∈ (0, δ/R); H is integrable and independent of r. Each h_r is measurable (indicator of the open set G_r times a function continuous on G_r).
7. (Pointwise limit.) Fix u ∈ ℝ^m. For r < ρ₀/(|u| + 1) we have u ∈ G_r. As r ↓ 0: ψ_r(u) = r^{-1}(ψ(v₀ + ru) − ψ(v₀)) → Au (differentiability of ψ at v₀), so f(ψ_r(u)) → f(Au) by continuity of f; and Dψ(v₀ + ru) → A (continuity of Dψ at v₀), so J(Dψ(v₀ + ru)) → J(A) by continuity of J. Hence h_r(u) → J(A) f(Au).
8. (Dominated convergence.) The filter r ↓ 0 (𝓝[>] 0) is countably generated; by steps 6–7 and the dominated convergence theorem (Mathlib tendsto_integral_filter_of_dominated_convergence), ∫ h_r du → J(A)∫_{ℝ^m} f(Au) du. By (4.2) and (5.1), lim_{r↓0} ∫_{η_{x,r}(N∩W)} f dH^m = J(A)∫_{ℝ^m} f(Au) du.
9. (The plane.) For the injective linear map A, H^m(A(S)) = J(A)·L^m(S) for every S ⊆ ℝ^m (Simon 3.1; Mathlib LinearMap.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_eq_normDet_mul_volume). As A is injective, A(A^{-1}(E)) = range A ∩ E, so H^m⌞range A is the image of J(A)·L^m under A, and ∫_{range A} f dH^m = J(A)∫_{ℝ^m} f(Au) du (f is continuous with compact support, so all integrals are finite). Since range A = Q (step 1), step 8 gives ∫_{η_{x,r}(N∩W)} f dH^m → ∫_Q f dH^m as r ↓ 0.
10. (Conclusion.) Steps 1 and 9 (f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P) arbitrary) are the two conjuncts of HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt m (N ∩ W) x Q. ∎
proof_key_steps: Chart (V, W₀, ψ) at x = ψ(v₀); chart_tangent_space gives Q = range Dψ(v₀) = range A, so dim Q = m.
Near v₀: |ψ(v) − ψ(v′)| ≥ (c₀/2)|v − v′| with c₀ = min_{|u|=1}|Au| > 0, and J(Dψ) ≤ C_J.
Properness and injectivity give δ > 0 with N ∩ B_δ(x) ⊆ ψ(B_{ρ₀}(v₀)) ∩ W.
For f supported in B_R(0) and r < δ/R, ∫_{η_{x,r}(N∩W)} f = ∫ 1_{G_r}(u) f(ψ_r(u)) J(Dψ(v₀ + ru)) du with ψ_r(u) = r^{-1}(ψ(v₀ + ru) − x) (area formula).
Dominated by sup|f|·C_J·1_{B_{2R/c₀}(0)}; pointwise limit J(A) f(Au); dominated convergence.
Linear area formula: J(A)∫ f(Au) du = ∫_{range A} f dH^m = ∫_Q f dH^m.

For a linear map L : U → ℝ^P on a finite-dimensional inner product space U, normDet(L) ≥ 0 is the Mathlib LinearMap.normDet: normDet(L)² = det(⟨Lb_i, Lb_j⟩) for every orthonormal basis b of U (LinearMap.normDet_sq_eq_det_gram); normDet(L) > 0 iff L is injective; normDet(g∘f) = normDet(g|_{range f})·normDet(f) (LinearMap.normDet_comp); L ↦ normDet(L) is continuous on maps ℝ^m → ℝ^P (SimonGMT Chapter02 continuous_normDet). L^m is Lebesgue measure on ℝ^m (= μHE[m] there).

Proof.
1. (J is a norm determinant.) For x ∈ ℝ^P let L_x : Q(x) → ℝ^P be the restriction of DΦ(x). Applying normDet_sq_eq_det_gram with the orthonormal basis e(x) of Q(x): J(x)² = det(⟨DΦ(x)e_i(x), DΦ(x)e_j(x)⟩) = normDet(L_x)², and both J(x) and normDet(L_x) are ≥ 0, so J(x) = normDet(L_x). In particular J(x) depends only on DΦ(x) and the subspace Q(x), and J(x) > 0 because L_x is injective.
2. (Chart formula.) Let (V, W₀, ψ) be a local representation of N (V ⊆ ℝ^m open, W₀ ⊆ ℝ^P open, ψ C¹ on V and injective on V, ψ(V) = W₀ ∩ N, proper, Dψ injective on V) and v ∈ V. By chart_tangent_space, Q(ψ(v)) = T_{ψ(v)}N = range Dψ(v). By the chain rule D(Φ∘ψ)(v) = DΦ(ψ(v))∘Dψ(v), and by normDet_comp and step 1 (the restriction of DΦ(ψ(v)) to range Dψ(v) = Q(ψ(v)) is L_{ψ(v)}):

3. (ψ is a homeomorphism onto W₀ ∩ N; Simon 4.2.) ψ maps V continuously and bijectively onto W₀ ∩ N. It is relatively closed: let F ⊆ V be closed in V and y_j = ψ(v_j) → y ∈ W₀ ∩ N with v_j ∈ F. The set K := {y} ∪ {y_j : j ≥ j₀} is compact and, for j₀ large, contained in W₀ (W₀ is an open neighbourhood of y), so the v_j (j ≥ j₀) lie in the compact set V ∩ ψ^{-1}(K); a subsequence converges to some v ∈ V ∩ ψ^{-1}(K), v ∈ F as F is closed in V, and ψ(v) = y. By (2.1), J∘ψ = normDet(D(Φ∘ψ))/normDet(Dψ) is continuous on V. By step 3, J = (J∘ψ)∘ψ^{-1} is continuous on W₀ ∩ N. W₀ ∩ N is a neighbourhood of each of its points relative to N (W₀ is open), so J is continuous within N at each point of W₀ ∩ N. The charts cover N, so J is continuous on N: the first conclusion.
5. (Φ is a measurable embedding.) Φ is continuous and injective on the Polish space ℝ^P, so by the Lusin–Souslin theorem it is a measurable embedding (Mathlib Continuous.measurableEmbedding): Φ(E) is Borel for Borel E, and ∫ g d(Φ_*μ) = ∫ g∘Φ dμ for every g : ℝ^P → [0, ∞] and every measure μ (MeasurableEmbedding.lintegral_map). N is covered by countably many chart sets W₀ ∩ N = ψ(V) (Lindelöf, ℝ^P second countable), each σ-compact (V is σ-compact and ψ continuous on V), so N is Borel (SimonGMT measurableSet_of_isSimonSubmanifold, after unfolding the contract's chart conditions into IsSimonSubmanifold). Comparing with (7.2): H^m(Φ(B)) = ∫_B J dH^m for every Borel B ⊆ W₀ ∩ N (take A := V ∩ ψ^{-1}(B), so ψ(A) = B).

By step 7 and countable additivity:

9. (Function formula.) Fix a Borel B ⊆ N. Let ν₁ := H^m⌞Φ(B) and ν₂ := Φ_*(J·(H^m⌞B)), where J·μ denotes the measure with density ofReal∘J. For Borel E, Φ(B) ∩ E = Φ(B ∩ Φ^{-1}(E)) (Φ injective) and B ∩ Φ^{-1}(E) is a Borel subset of N, so by (8.1) ν₁(E) = ∫_{B∩Φ^{-1}(E)} J dH^m = ν₂(E). Hence ν₁ = ν₂, and for every g : ℝ^P → [0, ∞]:
 ∫_{Φ(B)} g dH^m = ∫ g dν₁ = ∫ g dν₂ = ∫_B J·(g∘Φ) dH^m,

With ofReal(J(x)) in place of J(x) this is the asserted identity ∫⁻_{Φ(B)} g dH^m = ∫⁻_B ofReal(J(x))·g(Φ(x)) dH^m(x). ∎
